Answer: C
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates bilateral perihilar reticulo-nodular opacities and right paratracheal lymphadenopathy (widening of the right paratracheal stripe), which, combined with upper zone nodularity, forms the classic pattern for sarcoidosis. Bilateral pleural effusions (seen in options B, D, F) are rare in sarcoidosis and would suggest alternative diagnoses like heart failure or malignancy.
